podcast.title: Pre-Sloan Halifax Band
podcast.body: Carney Lake Road was an obscure pre-Sloan band from the Halifax area, featuring Jay Ferguson and Chris Murphy, who had been playing together since age seven. They gained early excitement from an appearance on "Indie Street" on Much Music, which aired at 3 AM on Sunday nights, after performing at venues like the Rivoli. "Starting with a group called Carney Lake Road. Very obscure. I don't expect anyone to know it. Jay and I were both in it."

xref.title: Formation and Longevity (1991)
xref.body: Sloan was formed in 1991, emerging from the Halifax area music scene after previous bands like Carney Lake Road. They are noted for their exceptional longevity, having existed since their formation. "Sloan. They were formed in 1991."

xref.title: Pre-Sloan Influencers and Tourmates
xref.body: The Straight Jackets were a Bedford-based band (part of a "New Brunswick experience") that headlined tours with Carney Lake Road. Their bass player, Jason Larson, had the nickname "Sloan," which was later adopted by the band Sloan, who even featured his face on their debut EP cover. "Straight Jackets was what they were called. They had a record out. It was very exciting."
